result.topic: External Vector DB vs MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
result.decision: Stay with MongoDB Atlas Vector Search as the exclusive vector store for both pipeline and frontend clusters. Do not introduce an external vector DB at this stage.
result.rationale: Boss has mandated continued investment in MongoDB Atlas to avoid operational overhead from additional services. Atlas Vector Search is sufficient for the current and near-term scale (up to 2M providers, 3072d vectors). RAM and performance issues are to be addressed by proper cluster sizing, index placement, and proactive monitoring.

vector_db_strategy.exclusive_use: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search (no Pinecone, Qdrant, or Azure Cognitive Search)
vector_db_strategy.index_placement: Vector indexes are created ONLY on the frontend cluster. Pipeline cluster holds raw vectors but no vector indexes.
vector_db_strategy.index_management: Index build and rebuild operations are run during off-peak hours. Indexes are versioned and old versions are dropped after successful migration.

action_on_threshold: Pause new vector writes if RAM > 90% until remediation

index_health.metric: Index build status, query latency, and failed search operations
index_health.alerting: Immediate alert if index build fails or search latency > 1s at p99

capacity_planning.review_interval: Monthly review of provider and vector counts vs RAM and storage utilization
capacity_planning.reporting: Dashboard and monthly report to CTO

action_on_breach: Trigger architecture review for external vector DB migration
Freeze new provider onboarding if RAM > 90% until scale-out or sharding is implemented

sharding_plan.shard_strategy: State-based sharding if provider count exceeds 2M or RAM exceeds 80%

result.topic: Parquet as Canonical Intermediate Format vs Direct CSV-to-MongoDB
result.decision: Adopt Parquet as the canonical intermediate format. All source CSVs are converted to Parquet before any downstream processing or MongoDB load.
result.rationale: Boss mandates Parquet for future-proofing and reliability. Parquet conversion must be explicit, reproducible, and partitioned for parallel downstream processing. This reduces CSV fragility and aligns with cloud-native best practices.

design_changes.conversion_point: CSV-to-Parquet conversion occurs immediately after download and integrity verification (ETag/SHA-256), before any partitioning or MongoDB load. All downstream processing (partitioning, chunking, enrichment) reads from Parquet, not CSV.
design_changes.library: pyarrow (Apache Arrow Python bindings) is the mandated library for conversion and Parquet I/O, due to maturity, performance, and ecosystem support.

partitioning_scheme.NPPES: Partitioned by state (state_abbr), year (file_version), and optionally by first letter of NPI for large states. Example path: nppes/state=CA/year=2026/npi_prefix=A/part-0001.parquet
partitioning_scheme.CMS_Part_D: Partitioned by state (state_abbr), year (file_version). Example path: cms_partd/state=NY/year=2026/part-0001.parquet
partitioning_scheme.OIG/SAM: Single partition per source per year unless file size > 1GB, then partition by hash prefix of NPI.
partitioning_scheme.crosswalk: Partitioned by molecule or indication as needed for parallel enrichment.

design_changes.byte_aligned_partitioning_interaction: For NPPES, byte-aligned CSV partitioning is replaced by row-based Parquet partitioning. Each Parquet file contains a row group aligned to the original CSV chunk boundaries (by row count, not byte offset). Partitioning logic is updated to operate on Parquet row groups.
design_changes.storage: All Parquet files are stored in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (ADLS Gen2) for hierarchical namespace and scalable throughput. Blob naming follows the partitioning scheme above.

monitoring_plan.conversion_success: Each CSV-to-Parquet conversion emits a conversion manifest (JSON) with row counts, schema fingerprint (SHA-256), and partition metadata. Failures are logged and block downstream steps.
monitoring_plan.parquet_integrity: After conversion, run pyarrow.parquet.ParquetFile validation and spot-check row counts vs CSV manifest.
monitoring_plan.storage_monitoring: Monitor ADLS Gen2 for available space, file count per partition, and throughput bottlenecks. Alert if any partition exceeds 10,000 files or 1TB.

scaling_guardrails.max_parquet_file_size: 512MB per file (row group), auto-split if larger
action_on_breach: Auto-merge small files if partition has >10,000 files
Alert and block pipeline if Parquet validation fails or storage quota exceeded

result.topic: Distributed Commit Log vs MongoDB-based Checkpointing
result.decision: Adopt a dual-logging system: (1) Continue using MongoDB admin.DataLoadMetadata for operational checkpoints. (2) Implement an append-only commit log using ADLS Gen2 append blobs. Do not introduce CosmosDB.
result.rationale: ADLS Gen2 append blobs are cost-effective, append-only, and fit naturally into our Azure-based pipeline. They avoid new service overhead and are queryable via Synapse or Databricks. This approach separates operational state (MongoDB) from the immutable audit trail (ADLS).

commit_log.entry_format: JSON Lines (one JSON object per line, UTF-8, no trailing commas)
commit_log.write_pattern: Each pipeline chunk promotion, stage completion, or critical event appends a new line atomically.
commit_log.retention: 365 days (configurable, with lifecycle policy for auto-delete)

checkpointing.write_pattern: Upsert per worker/chunk/stage, always latest state (idempotent)

fields.details: object (arbitrary event-specific metadata, e.g., record counts, hash values, error messages)
fields.schema_fingerprint: string (SHA-256 of schema at time of event, for drift detection)
fields.actor: string (service principal, user, or orchestrator id)

result.topic: Schema registry service vs schema-in-code
result.decision: Implement lightweight schema validation: fingerprint both the normalized schema object and the raw CSV header row. Store fingerprints in both admin.SchemaFingerprints (for historical tracking) and admin.DataLoadMetadata (per batch). On fingerprint mismatch, abort by default but allow override for hotfixes.
result.rationale: This approach balances safety (drift detection, audit trail) with simplicity. Storing in both places enables both per-batch and historical schema change tracking. Defaulting to abort prevents silent corruption, but override supports urgent production needs.

fingerprinted_items: 1. Raw CSV header row (as loaded, before normalization)
2. Normalized schema object (ordered list of field names and types, e.g., [{name: 'npi', type: 'string'}, ...])

on_fingerprint_mismatch.default: Hard abort pipeline step, raise alert to ops@chathealthy.ai, log event in commit log.
on_fingerprint_mismatch.override: Allow manual override via pipeline parameter (e.g., allow_schema_mismatch=true) for hotfixes. All overrides are logged and require explicit operator justification.

validation_function.signature: def validate_and_fingerprint_schema(raw_header: List[str], expected_normalized_schema: List[Dict[str, str]], allow_override: bool = False) -> Tuple[bool, str, str]
validation_function.description: Validates the raw CSV header and normalized schema against stored fingerprints. Returns (is_valid, raw_header_fingerprint, normalized_schema_fingerprint). Raises exception or aborts if mismatch and override is False.

steps: 1. Compute SHA-256 of raw_header (joined by comma, UTF-8).
2. Compute SHA-256 of normalized_schema (JSON-serialized, sorted keys, UTF-8).
3. Lookup expected fingerprints for source_name in admin.SchemaFingerprints.
4. If either fingerprint mismatches, abort unless allow_override is True.
5. If allow_override is True, log override event with justification.

result.topic: Complexity vs Pragmatism (Full Reliability Patterns NOW)
result.decision: Commit to a concrete, enforceable set of reliability patterns across all pipeline stages, effective immediately. All reliability mechanisms are specified with thresholds, implementation details, and enforcement points.
result.rationale: Boss mandates full reliability at current scale. This contract makes reliability non-negotiable and auditable, not aspirational.

thresholds.failure_rate: >= 5 consecutive failures OR >= 10% error rate in last 100 calls
thresholds.timeout: Any call > 10s triggers a soft failure; 3 timeouts in 5 minutes triggers breaker

circuit_breakers.breaker_behavior: On threshold breach, breaker opens for 10 minutes (no new requests, all attempts fail-fast). After 10 minutes, allow 1 probe call per minute until success. Log all breaker state changes to commit log and alert ops@chathealthy.ai.

dead_letter_queues.replay_policy: Scheduled retry job runs every 6 hours; max 3 retries per dead letter. Success moves record back to main pipeline; persistent failure escalates to ops.

retry_policies.scope: Per-call for all external API calls and chunk-level DB writes
retry_policies.backoff_formula: Exponential backoff with jitter: base_delay = 2s, max_delay = 60s, jitter = +/- 20%
retry_policies.global_limits: No more than 100 concurrent retries per pipeline stage to avoid stampede

scope: Simulate API timeouts and 500 errors for all external APIs
Randomly kill 5% of worker processes during enrichment and embedding
Inject random network latency (up to 2s) in 10% of chunk handoffs
chaos_testing.frequency: Nightly in dev and QA environments; monthly in prod with operator approval
chaos_testing.reporting: Chaos test results logged to admin.ChaosTestResults and summarized in monthly reliability report

operations_covered: Chunked data loads (upsert by NPI or unique key)
Enrichment steps (atomic update by _id and enrichment_status)

enforcement.idempotent_keys: All upserts use deterministic chunk IDs and unique keys (NPI, record_id, etc.)
enforcement.ETag/SHA-256 guards: No duplicate downloads or loads if ETag/SHA unchanged
enforcement.state_machine: Explicit chunk state: pending → in_progress → complete → verified | failed; only one transition per chunk at a time

result.topic: Parquet File Format and Pipeline Integration
result.decision: Specify concrete Parquet file conventions, row group sizing, compression, schema evolution, and writer interface.
result.rationale: These details ensure the Parquet layer is robust, scalable, and maintainable as the canonical intermediate format.

fields.state: Two-letter state abbreviation or 'ALL' if not state-specific
fields.version: Monotonic version for re-ingests on same day

row_group_size.rationale: 128MB row groups optimize for cloud read throughput and are compatible with Spark/Synapse. 500k rows is a secondary guard for variable-width records.

compression_codec.rationale: zstd offers better compression ratios and decompression speed than snappy or gzip, is natively supported by pyarrow, and is optimal for healthcare tabular data with moderate cardinality.

schema_evolution.strategy: Schema evolution is handled via Parquet's built-in support for optional columns. Each Parquet file stores the exact schema used for that batch in file metadata.
process: 1. On ingest, detect schema changes by comparing normalized schema fingerprint to previous batches.
2. If new columns are added, Parquet files include them as nullable fields.
3. If columns are dropped, they are omitted from new files; readers must handle missing fields as null.
4. All schema changes are logged in admin.SchemaFingerprints and referenced in the conversion manifest.
5. Downstream readers must use schema merging when reading multiple files across schema versions.
schema_evolution.backward_compatibility: Always prefer additive (new nullable columns) or reorder-tolerant changes. Breaking changes (type changes, column drops) require operator approval and are blocked by default.

__init__.description: Initialize writer with output path, schema, and config.

write_batch.description: Append a batch of records. Splits into row groups as needed.

finalize.description: Flush all buffers, close the Parquet file, and write manifest/metadata.

get_schema_fingerprint.description: Return the schema fingerprint for this file.

error_handling.on_schema_mismatch: Raise SchemaMismatchError and abort conversion unless allow_override is set.
error_handling.on_io_error: Retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff; log all failures to commit log and abort if persistent.
error_handling.on_partial_write: Write recovery marker and alert ops; do not proceed to downstream steps until resolved.

result.topic: Parquet ↔ MongoDB Data Flow, Source of Truth, Reconciliation, and Recovery
result.decision: Parquet is the canonical intermediate format in blob storage; MongoDB remains the queryable, operational state. Both are required for full pipeline function. Parquet enables robust cold-start recovery and auditability.
result.rationale: Parquet in ADLS Gen2 provides immutable, auditable, and partitioned storage for all ingested data. MongoDB is optimized for fast, flexible queries and downstream enrichment/embedding. This dual-path ensures resilience and operational agility.

data_flow.2_parquet_conversion: CSV converted to Parquet (partitioned, compressed, fingerprinted). Parquet files are written to ADLS Gen2.
data_flow.3_mongo_ingest: Parquet files are read in streaming batches and loaded into MongoDB collections (e.g., prod_provider_raw, prod_prescriber_raw). All downstream pipeline steps (enrichment, embedding, ship) operate on MongoDB.
data_flow.4_embedding: Embedding step reads from MongoDB, not Parquet. This ensures all enrichment and normalization is complete and leverages MongoDB's query/filter capabilities.
data_flow.5_ship: CopyToFrontEnd and all parity verification operate on MongoDB collections.

source_of_truth.blob_storage: Parquet in ADLS Gen2 is the immutable, auditable source of truth for raw and pre-processed data.
source_of_truth.mongodb: MongoDB is the mutable, queryable operational state for all active pipeline stages.

parquet_to_mongo: After each Parquet-to-MongoDB load, record counts and schema fingerprints are compared.
A reconciliation manifest is written per batch: {parquet_row_count, mongo_row_count, parquet_fingerprint, mongo_fingerprint, batch_id, timestamp}.
If counts or fingerprints mismatch, pipeline aborts and alerts ops.
Spot-check hash of first/last 1000 records in both Parquet and MongoDB for integrity.

result.embedding_step_read_path: Embedding workers always read from MongoDB, never directly from Parquet. This ensures they operate on fully enriched, normalized, and checkpointed records.

cold_start_recovery.scenario: If MongoDB is wiped or corrupted, pipeline can be rehydrated from Parquet in ADLS Gen2.
process: 1. Enumerate all Parquet files for the desired batch/date/partition.
2. Validate Parquet file integrity and schema fingerprints.
3. Replay Parquet-to-MongoDB load, reconstructing all raw collections.
4. Resume enrichment, embedding, and shipping as normal.
cold_start_recovery.limitations: Only data present in Parquet can be recovered. Downstream enrichment/embedding steps must be re-run unless their outputs are also checkpointed to Parquet (future enhancement).

result.topic: ADLS Commit Log Pathing, Sample Entries, Query, Retention, and Trace Correlation
result.decision: Define explicit ADLS commit log structure, sample entries, query methods, retention, and OpenTelemetry integration.
result.rationale: Clear commit log conventions enable reliable audit, troubleshooting, and traceability across pipeline runs.

notes: Each pipeline run writes to a single append blob (JSONL) for that run/date.
All events for the run are appended in order.

querying_commit_log.primary_method: Azure Synapse Analytics serverless SQL pool using OPENROWSET on ADLS Gen2 append blobs (JSONL).
alternative_methods: Direct read via pyarrow or pandas using fsspec/adlfs for targeted queries.
Databricks or Spark cluster for large-scale analysis.
querying_commit_log.indexing_note: For high-frequency queries, consider periodic ETL to a query-optimized store (e.g., Azure Data Explorer) in future.

retention_policy.enforcement: Azure Blob Lifecycle Management policy auto-deletes commit log blobs after 365 days.
retention_policy.override: Retention can be extended for compliance or audit requirements by updating the lifecycle policy.

commit_log_and_opentelemetry.correlation: Each commit log entry includes an otel_trace_id field (OpenTelemetry trace context).
integration: This enables cross-system correlation between pipeline events and distributed traces.
Operators can trace a chunk or stage event from the commit log to full distributed traces in the OpenTelemetry backend (e.g., Azure Monitor, Jaeger).
commit_log_and_opentelemetry.best_practice: All pipeline workers and orchestrators propagate the current OpenTelemetry trace context when emitting commit log entries.

result.topic: MongoDB Checkpointing (admin.DataLoadMetadata) and Commit Log Cross-Reference
result.decision: Define explicit MongoDB checkpoint schema, provide sample documents, and specify reconciliation logic with commit log.
result.rationale: Precise checkpointing enables deterministic recovery, chunk-level monitoring, and cross-system audit with the commit log.

fields.commit_log_ref: string (ADLS path to related commit log entry, e.g., 'commit_logs/provider_pipeline/2026/04/08/commitlog_...jsonl:12345')

checkpoint_commit_log_cross_reference.mechanism: Each checkpoint document includes a commit_log_ref field, which points to the ADLS path and line offset (or event id) of the corresponding commit log entry for the most recent state transition.
checkpoint_commit_log_cross_reference.write_pattern: When a worker transitions chunk state (e.g., completes a chunk), it writes the commit log entry first, then updates the checkpoint document with the commit_log_ref.

reconciliation_query.description: Find all chunks that have a 'chunk_complete' event in the commit log but no corresponding checkpoint document in MongoDB.
steps: 1. Use Synapse or Spark to extract all chunk_id and pipeline_run_id from commit log entries where event_type = 'chunk_complete'.
2. Query admin.DataLoadMetadata for documents with matching pipeline_run_id and chunk_id, state='complete'.
3. Return all (pipeline_run_id, chunk_id) pairs present in the commit log but missing in MongoDB.
reconciliation_query.pseudo_sql: SELECT c.pipeline_run_id, c.chunk_id FROM commit_log c WHERE c.event_type = 'chunk_complete' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM admin.DataLoadMetadata m WHERE m.pipeline_run_id = c.pipeline_run_id AND m.chunk_id = c.chunk_id AND m.state = 'complete')

result.topic: Full Reliability Pattern Implementation for v3
result.decision: Specify all reliability mechanisms with concrete state machines, schemas, schedules, and fallback logic.
result.rationale: Explicit implementation details ensure reliability is not left to interpretation and can be validated in code and operations.

transitions: closed → open: On threshold breach (see below)
open → half-open: After reset timeout expires
half-open → closed: On first successful probe call
half-open → open: On probe call failure

thresholds.failure_rate: >= 5 consecutive failures OR >= 10% error rate in last 100 calls
thresholds.timeout: Any call > 10s counts as failure; 3 timeouts in 5 minutes triggers open

implementation.shared_state: One breaker per external API endpoint
implementation.logging: All state transitions logged to commit log and alert ops@chathealthy.ai

retry_schedule.scheduler: Azure Function TimerTrigger or Durable Entity
retry_schedule.on_success: Move record back to main pipeline

poison_message_handling.action: Mark as poison, alert ops, do not retry further, require manual intervention

rate_limiter.implementation: Distributed token bucket (Redis or in-memory per worker with periodic sync)
rate_limiter.enforcement: All API calls must acquire token before execution; if unavailable, wait or fail-fast if circuit breaker is open

checks: MongoDB cluster status (primary/replica health, storage usage)
ADLS Gen2 container access and free space
health_checks.alerting: Immediate email to ops@chathealthy.ai and dashboard update

optional_enrichments: Google Maps Geocoding (practice and billing address, paid, optional)
NPPES public registry lookup by NPI (last pass, optional if circuit breaker is open)
required_enrichments: Census Geocoder (at least one address per provider)

criteria: All records have ZIP-based county crosswalk
At least one successful Census Geocoder pass per provider
fallback_behavior: If optional enrichments fail (circuit breaker open), log all skipped IDs to dead letter and proceed
Pipeline only aborts if required enrichments cannot be completed

result.topic: Ensuring Commit Log and MongoDB Checkpoint Consistency
result.decision: Implement a two-phase commit pattern with periodic reconciliation and explicit recovery procedures.
result.rationale: Dual logging introduces the risk of divergence. A disciplined write order, reconciliation job, and operator alerts are required to maintain auditability and operational safety.

write_order: 1. Write commit log entry to ADLS append blob (commit_logs/...).
2. On successful commit log write, update MongoDB checkpoint (admin.DataLoadMetadata) with commit_log_ref.

3. If MongoDB update fails after commit log write, retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff. If still failing, alert ops and mark chunk as 'checkpoint_pending' in a special admin.CheckpointPending collection.

commit_log_write_fails_first.action: Do NOT update MongoDB checkpoint. Worker retries commit log write up to 3 times (with backoff). If still failing, chunk remains in 'in_progress' state and is picked up for retry by the reconciliation job.

commit_log_write_succeeds_but_mongo_chec.action: Retry MongoDB checkpoint up to 3 times. If still failing, log to admin.CheckpointPending and alert ops. The reconciliation job will attempt to re-apply the checkpoint using the commit log as the source of truth.

reconciliation_job.description: A scheduled job (Azure Function TimerTrigger) runs every 15 minutes to compare commit log and checkpoint state.
steps: 1. Enumerate all 'chunk_complete' events in commit log for the last 24 hours.
2. For each, check for a corresponding 'complete' checkpoint in admin.DataLoadMetadata.
3. If commit log entry exists but no checkpoint, attempt to re-apply the checkpoint using the commit log details.
4. If checkpoint exists but no commit log entry, flag as 'commit_log_missing' in admin.CheckpointPending and alert ops.
5. All reconciliation actions are logged to admin.ReconciliationLog.

commit_log_missing.description: Checkpoint exists but no commit log entry.
action: 1. Attempt to reconstruct the missing commit log entry from checkpoint and pipeline context.
2. Write reconstructed entry to commit log with a 'recovered' flag.
3. Alert ops for manual review if reconstruction is ambiguous.

checkpoint_missing.description: Commit log entry exists but no MongoDB checkpoint.
action: 1. Attempt to re-apply the checkpoint to MongoDB using commit log details.
2. If re-apply fails, alert ops and mark chunk as 'checkpoint_recovery_failed' in admin.CheckpointPending.

operator_alerts: All reconciliation failures and recovery attempts are emailed to ops@chathealthy.ai.
Dashboard displays all chunks in 'checkpoint_pending', 'commit_log_missing', or 'checkpoint_recovery_failed' state for operator action.

result.topic: Testing Strategy for Reliability Patterns
result.decision: Implement a comprehensive, automated reliability testing suite covering all critical failure and recovery paths, with continuous and pre-release chaos testing.
result.rationale: Reliability patterns must be validated by simulation, not assumption. Automated, repeatable tests catch regressions and ensure operational readiness.

circuit_breaker_testing.method: Mock failure injection at the API client layer for each external API (Census, Google Maps, RxNorm, NPPES).
scenarios: Inject HTTP 500/timeout for N consecutive calls to trigger breaker.
Verify breaker transitions to open, then half-open, then closed after reset timer and probe success.
Log all state transitions and assert correct alerting.
circuit_breaker_testing.automation: Nightly in dev/QA, before every release in prod.

checkpoint_restart_testing.method: Simulate worker/process termination mid-chunk (SIGKILL or Azure Function scale-down).
scenarios: Kill worker during chunk processing; verify orchestrator detects expired heartbeat and reassigns chunk.
Restart pipeline from arbitrary stage using start_step; verify no data loss and idempotent completion.
checkpoint_restart_testing.automation: Nightly in dev/QA, weekly in prod.

parquet_corruption_testing.method: Inject corrupted Parquet files (truncated, bad CRC, schema mismatch) into ADLS test partitions.
scenarios: Attempt Parquet-to-MongoDB load from bad files; verify pipeline aborts, logs error, and alerts ops.
Test recovery by replacing with valid file and resuming pipeline.
parquet_corruption_testing.automation: Weekly in dev/QA, pre-release in prod.

chaos_testing_schedule.prod: Monthly, with operator approval and rollback plan. Pre-release full chaos suite mandatory.

dual_logging_reconciliation_testing.method: Inject artificial commit log or checkpoint write failures (e.g., block ADLS or MongoDB writes for selected chunks).
scenarios: Force commit log write to fail, verify checkpoint is not written and chunk is retried.
Force checkpoint write to fail after commit log succeeds, verify reconciliation job recovers state.
Delete or corrupt commit log/checkpoint entries and verify reconciliation job detects and repairs or alerts.
dual_logging_reconciliation_testing.automation: Nightly in dev/QA; pre-release in prod.

reporting.all_failures: Logged to admin.TestFailureLog with scenario, timestamp, and outcome.
reporting.dashboard: Reliability test pass/fail status and coverage displayed on operator dashboard.
reporting.alerts: Critical test failures (e.g., data loss, unrecoverable state) trigger immediate ops alert.

result.topic: Pipeline Failure, Data Corruption, Dual Logging Disagreement, Alerting, SLA
result.decision: Define explicit runbooks for major operational incidents, alerting targets, and pipeline SLA.
result.rationale: Clear, actionable runbooks and alerting reduce MTTR and ensure compliance with reliability commitments.

pipeline_run_failure: 1. Alert: Immediate email and dashboard alert to ops@chathealthy.ai and on-call engineer (PagerDuty integration) on any pipeline abort or unhandled exception.
2. Diagnosis: Operator reviews failure logs in admin.DataLoadMetadata and commit log for error context.
3. Checkpoint Review: Identify last successful chunk/stage from checkpoints.
4. Data Consistency: Run reconciliation query to ensure no partial chunks are marked complete.
5. Remediation: Address root cause (e.g., fix code, resolve quota, restart failed service).
6. Resume: Restart pipeline using start_step parameter at last successful stage/chunk.
7. Postmortem: Log incident in admin.IncidentLog and update runbook if new failure mode discovered.
parquet_file_corruption: 1. Alert: Immediate alert to ops@chathealthy.ai and dashboard if Parquet validation fails during load.
2. Quarantine: Move corrupted Parquet file to /corrupted/ partition in ADLS Gen2.
3. Diagnosis: Operator inspects file integrity (e.g., pyarrow validation, CRC check, schema mismatch).
4. Recovery: If possible, re-convert original CSV to Parquet and replace corrupted file.
5. Resume: Re-run Parquet-to-MongoDB load for affected partition.
6. Escalation: If original source is unavailable, escalate to data provider and document in admin.IncidentLog.
commit_log_checkpoint_disagreement: 1. Alert: Immediate alert to ops@chathealthy.ai and dashboard if reconciliation job detects mismatch.
2. Diagnosis: Operator reviews admin.CheckpointPending and commit log entries for affected chunk(s).
3. Recovery Path A (commit log exists, checkpoint missing): Re-apply checkpoint using commit log details.
4. Recovery Path B (checkpoint exists, commit log missing): Attempt to reconstruct and append missing commit log entry; flag as 'recovered'.
5. Manual Review: If automated recovery fails, escalate for manual operator intervention.
6. Documentation: Log all actions in admin.ReconciliationLog and update runbook if new scenario is found.

alerts_fired: Circuit breaker open for required enrichment
Health check failure (API, MongoDB, ADLS, backlog)
recipients: CTO (daily summary and all SLA breaches)

pipeline_sla.completion_time: 24 hours from scheduled start for all standard pipeline runs
enforcement: SLA timer starts at scheduled pipeline kickoff (UTC).
If pipeline not complete within 24h, critical alert to CTO and ops.
All SLA breaches logged in admin.SLABreachLog with root cause and remediation.
exceptions: Force majeure (cloud outage, upstream data delay) documented and excluded from SLA calculation.

result.topic: Exceptional Scenarios and Pipeline Safeguards
result.decision: Define explicit behaviors and safeguards for major edge cases in pipeline operation.
result.rationale: Edge cases are a primary source of silent data loss or corruption. Explicit handling ensures resilience and operator clarity.

nppes_mid_month_correction.detection: Correction file detected by new ETag/SHA-256 in DataFetcherBase manifest.
ingest_behavior: Treat as new pipeline run with incremented version (e.g., v2 for same month).
Parquet and MongoDB collections use versioned suffix (e.g., nppes_CA_20260408_v2_part0001.parquet, prod_provider_raw_v2).
Previous run's data is archived but retained for audit.
nppes_mid_month_correction.operator_alert: Alert ops@chathealthy.ai and dashboard on correction detection; require operator approval to promote corrected data to frontend.

cms_partd_file_format_change.detection: Schema fingerprint mismatch during pre-ingest dry run.
ingest_behavior: Pipeline aborts with hard error and alert.
If compatible (additive/reorder), operator can override and proceed.
If breaking (type/field drop), code/schema update required before ingest.
cms_partd_file_format_change.operator_alert: Immediate alert to ops@chathealthy.ai and CTO.

pipeline_cluster_disk_full.detection: Health check detects <10% free disk or MongoDB storage alert.
ingest_behavior: Pipeline pauses all new chunk processing.
Operator must free space (archive/delete old collections, scale storage, or expand disk).
Pipeline resumes automatically when >20% free disk.
pipeline_cluster_disk_full.prevention: Weekly storage audit and auto-prune of expired data (per retention policy).

azure_blob_storage_regional_outage.detection: Health check fails to access ADLS Gen2 for >5 minutes.
ingest_behavior: Pipeline enters 'paused' state; all workers halt new writes/reads.
Automatic retry every 10 minutes until storage is reachable.
Pipeline resumes from last checkpoint when storage returns.
azure_blob_storage_regional_outage.operator_action: If outage >2 hours, escalate to Azure support and document in admin.IncidentLog.

prevention: Pipeline orchestrator enforces exclusive lock per pipeline_name and data version (e.g., provider_pipeline:20260408:v1).
If new run is triggered while another is active on same data/version, new run is queued or rejected with operator alert.
allowed_overlap: Runs on different data versions (e.g., v1 and v2 for mid-month correction) are allowed, but write to separate Parquet/MongoDB partitions.
Operator review required before promoting overlapping runs to frontend.
overlapping_pipeline_runs.operator_alert: Alert ops@chathealthy.ai and dashboard if overlap is attempted.

result.focus: Security and Compliance for Parquet, Commit Log, and Access Control
result.topic: Data Protection, RBAC, and Compliance in v3 Pipeline
result.decision: Enforce encryption, access controls, and audit logging for all PII-containing artifacts. Align retention and access with compliance requirements.
result.rationale: Healthcare data pipelines must meet HIPAA, SOC 2, and internal security standards. Explicit controls for PII, audit, and access are non-negotiable.

parquet_files_encryption.encryption_at_rest: All Parquet files are stored in ADLS Gen2 containers with Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) using Microsoft-managed keys by default.

result.focus: Migration Path from v2 to v3 (Parquet Canonical)
result.topic: Migration, Coexistence, Rollback, and Timeline
result.decision: Adopt a side-by-side (blue/green) migration with dual-write and explicit rollback, minimizing risk and downtime.
result.rationale: A phased, reversible migration allows for validation, operational continuity, and rapid rollback if issues arise.

steps: 1. Enable Parquet conversion in parallel with existing CSV-to-MongoDB ingest. For each pipeline run, write both Parquet files (to ADLS Gen2) and load to MongoDB as before.
2. Validate Parquet output: Run schema fingerprint, row count, and hash spot checks between Parquet and MongoDB collections for each chunk.
3. Update downstream pipeline stages (enrichment, embedding, ship) to optionally read from Parquet for test runs, but keep MongoDB as operational source in production.
4. Run both v2 and v3 pipelines in parallel for at least 2 full cycles (e.g., 2 monthly NPPES/CMS loads). Compare outputs for parity.
5. Monitor for discrepancies: Use reconciliation manifests and dashboards to track any drift or data loss.
6. Operator sign-off: Once v3 Parquet pipeline output is validated as equivalent or superior, switch operational pipeline to use Parquet as canonical source for all new runs.
7. Retire v2: After 30 days of stable v3 operation, decommission CSV-to-MongoDB ingest and drop legacy code paths.

rollback_plan.trigger: If v3 Parquet pipeline fails or produces inconsistent results during migration window.
actions: 1. Immediately revert to v2 pipeline (CSV-to-MongoDB only).
2. Retain all CSV and MongoDB raw collections for at least 60 days post-migration.
3. Investigate and resolve root cause in v3 before retrying migration.
4. Document incident and update migration runbook.

migration_window.duration: Minimum 2 pipeline cycles (typically 2 months for NPPES/CMS), up to 3 months maximum.
criteria_to_cutover: No data loss or corruption detected in v3 output.
All operational dashboards and reconciliations show parity.

coexistence_notes: Dual-write (CSV-to-MongoDB and Parquet) incurs minimal extra cost at current scale.
All monitoring, reconciliation, and alerting must cover both v2 and v3 paths during migration window.
Downstream consumers are not switched to Parquet until full cutover.

result.overview: v3 introduces Parquet as the canonical intermediate format, dual logging (commit log + MongoDB checkpoint), and full reliability patterns. result.title: Pipeline Architecture v3 -- Final Canonical Design (Claude + GPT-4.1)
result.overview: v3 establishes Parquet as the canonical intermediate format, implements dual logging (ADLS commit log + MongoDB checkpoint), and mandates full reliability patterns. All previously parked items are resolved per Boss's direction. The pipeline is ready for 50-state scale, with explicit migration, rollback, and operational runbooks.
priority_goals: 1. RELIABILITY -- pipeline must complete or resume from last checkpoint. No data loss. Parity verification mandatory.
2. SPEED -- parallel where possible. Fan-out per state. Download in parallel. Process in parallel.
3. COST -- minimize compute time on Azure Functions. Minimize MongoDB Atlas cluster uptime. Pause when not running.
4. COMPLIANCE -- full audit trail, encryption at rest, RBAC, and PII minimization.
